# Overview

This file is the single place where **all** datasets consumed by the rapid app
are prepped and written. Every object written here lands in the app repo. For
now that is `../nps_wsva_app/prototypes/app_data/`, which the Methods Explorer
reads, so the deployed app's `app_data/` is left as it is (see `dir_app` in
section 0).

| Output | Contents |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `final_indicators.csv` | One row per water supply, one column per indicator (raw values). Also saved as `data/rapid/outputs/final_indicators_<date>.csv`. |
| `supply_indicator_weights.csv` | One row per water supply: its source category and one `wt_<indicator>` weight (0-1) per indicator. Also saved as `data/rapid/outputs/supply_indicator_weights_<date>.csv`. |
| `water_supplies.csv` | Water supply attributes + state water rights doctrine |
| `wbm_data.gpkg` | LOCA2 climate change summary, spatialized |
| `municipal_hauled.gpkg` | Municipal / hauled / tribal / purchased supplies |

Indicator values are written as **raw** (un-normalized) values. The app
re-normalizes and aggregates them on the fly via `calc_vulnerability_index()`,
so normalization must stay out of this file.

**Source-type weights:** section 3 also writes each supply's indicator weights
(`supply_indicator_weights.csv`). They are applied after normalizing, so the
indicator values written here stay raw and unweighted. Only the Methods
Explorer prototype applies them; the deployed app does not.

**Index hierarchy (calculated in the app, not here):** Indicators to Vulnerability
Factors to Components (Exposure / Sensitivity) to Total Vulnerability Index,
following the Euclidean distance framework of
[Michalak et al. (2021)](https://irma.nps.gov/DataStore/Reference/Profile/2287636).

# 0. Paths and helpers

```{r paths-helpers}
# All paths are relative to project root (set in the setup chunk)
dir_out <- "data/rapid/outputs"   # date-stamped indicator outputs
# Where the outputs go, in a clone of nps_wsva_app next to this repo. For now
# this is the prototypes' data folder, read by the Methods Explorer, so the
# deployed app's data is left as it is. Switch to "../nps_wsva_app/app_data"
# when the deployed app is ready for the updated indicators.
dir_app <- "../nps_wsva_app/prototypes/app_data"
dir_int <- "data/rapid"           # intermediate / archive products

dir.create(dir_app, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)


#' Most recent date-stamped file for a given stem
#'
#' Matches `<stem>_YYYY-MM-DD.<ext>` anchored at both ends, so files with extra
#' leading or trailing text (e.g. `kw_runoff_exposure_...`,
#' `..._moderate_...`) are excluded automatically.
#'
#' @param stem file name stem, e.g. "runoff_exposure"
#' @param dir directory to search
#' @param ext file extension, without the dot
#' @return full path to the most recent match, or NA_character_ if none
latest_file <- function(stem, dir = dir_out, ext = "csv") {
  files <- list.files(
    dir,
    pattern = paste0("^", stem, "_\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\\.", ext, "$"),
    full.names = TRUE
  )
  if (length(files) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  dates <- as.Date(str_extract(basename(files), "\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}"))
  files[which.max(dates)]
}
```

# 1. Indicator registry

**This tibble is the only place to edit when an indicator is added, renamed, or
retired.** Everything downstream (which files get read, which columns get kept,
what they are called in the app, and the column order of
`final_indicators.csv`) is derived from it.

To add a new indicator:

1.  Add a row below with the app-facing name, the raw column name in the output
    file, and the file stem.
2.  Knit. The validation chunk reports anything that did not land.
3.  Add a row to `weights/indicator_weights.csv` (skip for `_model_agree`
    columns, which are confidence weights and are never source-type weighted).
    The weights chunk in section 3 stops if a scored indicator has no row there.
4.  Add a matching row to `app_data/indicator_details.csv` in `nps_wsva_app` (label,
    description, direction, status) and to `indicator_config` in `app.R`.

The list below follows the Impact Pathways table in the Phase 1 revisions notes
(Pathway > Component > Factor > Indicator).

Conventions:

-   `app_name` prefix is `exp_` (Exposure) or `sen_` (Sensitivity).
-   Keep existing `app_name`s stable: the app's `calc_vulnerability_index()`
    looks columns up by name and quietly treats a missing one as NA (or, for a
    `_model_agree` column, as a weight of 1).
-   `source_col` is always a `raw_` column. Do not register `norm_` columns.
-   Model-agreement columns must be **fraction scale (0-1)**, not percent, or
    they will swamp the amount indicators during aggregation.
-   For multi-metric outputs, pick the percentile that is most vulnerable:
    `p10` for runoff / precip / SWE / drought (largest decrease), `p90` for
    everything else (largest increase).
-   Extreme precipitation and dry-spell indicators use **percent** change,
    except the counts of very wet days (`pr99days`) and summer days (`su`),
    which use the change in **days**: their historical baselines are near zero
    in many places, so percent change blows up (up to ~1,000% or more).

```{r indicator-registry}
indicator_registry <- tribble(
  ~app_name,                              ~source_col,                                     ~file_stem,                           ~pathway,          ~component,    ~factor,

  # ---- WATER QUANTITY ------------------------------------------------------
  # Exposure / Water Supply: % change in runoff/precip (runoff for most sources,
  # precip for rainwater; the app picks the branch by source type)
  "exp_runoff_change",                    "raw_runoff_change_p10",                         "runoff_exposure",                    "Water Quantity",  "Exposure",    "Water Supply",
  "exp_runoff_model_agree",               "raw_runoff_models_showing_decrease",            "runoff_exposure",                    "Water Quantity",  "Exposure",    "Water Supply",
  "exp_precip_change",                    "raw_precipitation_change_p10",                  "precipitation_exposure",             "Water Quantity",  "Exposure",    "Water Supply",
  "exp_precip_model_agree",               "raw_precip_models_showing_decrease",            "precipitation_exposure",             "Water Quantity",  "Exposure",    "Water Supply",
  # Exposure / Water Supply: projected change in runoff/precip timing
  "exp_runoff_timing_change",             "raw_runoff_timing_change_magnitude",            "runoff_timing_exposure",             "Water Quantity",  "Exposure",    "Water Supply",
  "exp_runoff_timing_change_model_agree", "raw_runoff_timing_direction_agreement_fraction","runoff_timing_exposure",             "Water Quantity",  "Exposure",    "Water Supply",
  "exp_precip_timing_change",             "raw_precip_timing_change_magnitude",            "precip_timing_exposure",             "Water Quantity",  "Exposure",    "Water Supply",
  "exp_precip_timing_change_model_agree", "raw_precip_timing_direction_agreement_fraction","precip_timing_exposure",             "Water Quantity",  "Exposure",    "Water Supply",
  # Exposure / Drought: change in SPEI (negative = drier = more vulnerable)
  "exp_drought_change",                   "raw_spei_change_p10",                           "drought_exposure",                   "Water Quantity",  "Exposure",    "Drought",
  "exp_drought_model_agree",              "raw_spei_models_showing_decrease",              "drought_exposure",                   "Water Quantity",  "Exposure",    "Drought",
  # Sensitivity / Water Supply: historical trend in runoff/precip
  "sen_runoff_trend",                     "raw_slope_runoff",                              "runoff_sensitivity",                 "Water Quantity",  "Sensitivity", "Water Supply",
  "sen_precip_trend",                     "raw_slope_precip",                              "precip_sensitivity",                 "Water Quantity",  "Sensitivity", "Water Supply",
  # Sensitivity / Drought: historical trend in SPEI
  "sen_drought_trend",                    "raw_slope_spei",                                "drought_sensitivity",                "Water Quantity",  "Sensitivity", "Drought",

  # ---- WATER DEMAND --------------------------------------------------------
  # Exposure / Demand
  "exp_nearby_use_change",                "raw_use_change_p90",                            "nearby_use_exposure",                "Water Demand",    "Exposure",    "Demand",
  "exp_nearby_use_model_agree",           "raw_models_showing_increase_pct",               "nearby_use_exposure",                "Water Demand",    "Exposure",    "Demand",
  "exp_auc_change",                       "raw_timing_change_p90",                         "timing_mismatch_exposure_Pred_High", "Water Demand",    "Exposure",    "Demand",
  # Sensitivity / Demand. Nearby water use is now the current (average) use per
  # km2, not the trend (Tyler's edits; the trend column is no longer written).
  # The app name stays sen_competition so the app keeps finding it.
  "sen_competition",                      "raw_avg_nearby_use_per_km2",                    "nearby_use_sensitivity",             "Water Demand",    "Sensitivity", "Demand",
  "sen_auc_change",                       "raw_timing_mismatch_auc",                       "timing_mismatch_sensitivity",        "Water Demand",    "Sensitivity", "Demand",
  "sen_visitation_trend",                 "raw_scaled_trend_visitation",                   "visitation_sensitivity",             "Water Demand",    "Sensitivity", "Demand",

  # ---- FLOOD ---------------------------------------------------------------
  # Exposure / Flood: extreme precipitation (LOCA2 extremes, written by the
  # flood exposure calc to flood_exposure_<date>.csv)
  "exp_extreme_precip_1day",              "raw_prmax1day_percent_change_p90",              "flood_exposure",                     "Flood",           "Exposure",    "Flood",
  "exp_extreme_precip_1day_model_agree",  "raw_prmax1day_models_showing_increase",         "flood_exposure",                     "Flood",           "Exposure",    "Flood",
  "exp_extreme_precip_5day",              "raw_prmax5day_percent_change_p90",              "flood_exposure",                     "Flood",           "Exposure",    "Flood",
  "exp_extreme_precip_5day_model_agree",  "raw_prmax5day_models_showing_increase",         "flood_exposure",                     "Flood",           "Exposure",    "Flood",
  "exp_extreme_precip_days",              "raw_pr99days_change_p90",                       "flood_exposure",                     "Flood",           "Exposure",    "Flood",
  "exp_extreme_precip_days_model_agree",  "raw_pr99days_models_showing_increase",          "flood_exposure",                     "Flood",           "Exposure",    "Flood",
  # Sensitivity / Flood: FEMA SFHA (100-yr flood)
  "sen_flood_risk",                       "raw_flood_risk_percent",                        "flood_sensitivity",                  "Flood",           "Sensitivity", "Flood",

  # ---- WILDFIRE ------------------------------------------------------------
  "exp_fire_prob_change",                 "raw_fire_prob_change_p90",                      "fire_exposure",                      "Wildfire",        "Exposure",    "Wildfire",
  "exp_fire_model_agree",                 "raw_fire_models_showing_increase",              "fire_exposure",                      "Wildfire",        "Exposure",    "Wildfire",
  "sen_wildfire_hazard",                  "raw_wildfire_hazard_mean",                      "fire_sensitivity",                   "Wildfire",        "Sensitivity", "Wildfire",

  # ---- COASTAL IMPACTS -----------------------------------------------------
  "exp_inundation_slr",                   "raw_pct_point_change",                          "inundation_exposure",                "Coastal Impacts", "Exposure",    "Coastal Impacts",
  "exp_storm_surge",                      "raw_surge_change_max",                          "storm_surge_exposure",               "Coastal Impacts", "Exposure",    "Coastal Impacts",
  "exp_swi",                              "raw_swi_migration",                             "swi_exposure",                       "Coastal Impacts", "Exposure",    "Coastal Impacts",
  "sen_inundation_current",               "raw_coverage_pct_ref",                          "inundation_exposure",                "Coastal Impacts", "Sensitivity", "Coastal Impacts",

  # ---- WATER QUALITY -------------------------------------------------------
  # Exposure / Water Quality: change in extreme temperature days (summer days,
  # Tmax > 25 C) and consecutive dry days
  "exp_extreme_temp_days",                "raw_su_change_p90",                             "temp_threshold_exposure",            "Water Quality",   "Exposure",    "Water Quality",
  "exp_extreme_temp_days_model_agree",    "raw_su_models_showing_increase",                "temp_threshold_exposure",            "Water Quality",   "Exposure",    "Water Quality",
  "exp_dry_days",                         "raw_cdd_percent_change_p90",                    "dry_period_exposure",                "Water Quality",   "Exposure",    "Water Quality",
  "exp_dry_days_model_agree",             "raw_cdd_change_models_showing_increase",        "dry_period_exposure",                "Water Quality",   "Exposure",    "Water Quality",
  # Sensitivity / Water Quality
  "sen_treatment_capacity",               "raw_treatment_capacity",                        "treatment_capacity_sensitivity",     "Water Quality",   "Sensitivity", "Water Quality"

  # ---- NOT YET WIRED (uncomment when the output exists) --------------------
  # NOTE: add a trailing comma to the row above before uncommenting any of these
  # "exp_swe_change",       "raw_swe_change_p10",              "swe_exposure", "Water Quantity", "Exposure", "Water Supply",
  # "exp_swe_model_agree",  "raw_swe_models_showing_decrease", "swe_exposure", "Water Quantity", "Exposure", "Water Supply",
)

# Guard against copy-paste duplicates in the registry itself
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(indicator_registry$app_name),
  !anyDuplicated(indicator_registry$source_col)
)

count(indicator_registry, pathway, component, factor)
```

# 2. Assemble indicators

Read the most recent output file for every stem in the registry, keep only the
registered raw columns, and full-join on `wsd_source_id`.

Each file is de-duplicated to one row per `wsd_source_id` **before** joining, so
a duplicated row in any single output cannot fan out the joined table.

```{r read-indicator-files}
indicator_files <- tibble(file_stem = unique(indicator_registry$file_stem)) |>
  mutate(file = map_chr(file_stem, latest_file))

# Report (do not silently drop) stems with no matching output file
missing_files <- filter(indicator_files, is.na(file))
if (nrow(missing_files) > 0) {
  warning("No date-stamped file found for: ",
          paste(missing_files$file_stem, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
}

indicator_files <- filter(indicator_files, !is.na(file))

# Which file / date each indicator is coming from this run
indicator_files |>
  mutate(file_date = str_extract(basename(file), "\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}")) |>
  select(file_stem, file_date) |>
  arrange(file_stem) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

```{r assemble-indicators}
wanted_cols <- indicator_registry$source_col

indicator_list <- indicator_files$file |>
  set_names(indicator_files$file_stem) |>
  map(\(f) {
    read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
      select(wsd_source_id, any_of(wanted_cols)) |>
      distinct(wsd_source_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
  })

# Fail loudly on cross-file column collisions rather than getting silent .x/.y
col_map <- imap(
  indicator_list,
  \(df, nm) tibble(file_stem = nm, source_col = setdiff(names(df), "wsd_source_id"))
) |>
  list_rbind()

collisions <- col_map |> count(source_col) |> filter(n > 1)
if (nrow(collisions) > 0) {
  stop("Same raw column supplied by more than one file: ",
       paste(collisions$source_col, collapse = ", "),
       ". Rename it upstream in the calc_* script.", call. = FALSE)
}

indicators_assembled <- reduce(indicator_list, full_join, by = "wsd_source_id")

dim(indicators_assembled)
```

## Validation

```{r validate-registry}
# Registry rows that never landed: bad stem, bad column name, or missing file
not_found <- indicator_registry |>
  filter(!source_col %in% names(indicators_assembled)) |>
  select(app_name, source_col, file_stem)

if (nrow(not_found) > 0) {
  warning(nrow(not_found), " registered indicator(s) not found in any output file.",
          call. = FALSE)
  print(not_found)
} else {
  cat("All", nrow(indicator_registry), "registered indicators found.\n")
}

# Confirm the file each column actually came from matches the registry
mismatched_stems <- indicator_registry |>
  inner_join(col_map, by = "source_col", suffix = c("_registry", "_actual")) |>
  filter(file_stem_registry != file_stem_actual) |>
  select(app_name, source_col, file_stem_registry, file_stem_actual)

if (nrow(mismatched_stems) > 0) {
  message("Registry `file_stem` is out of date for these rows (values are still correct):")
  print(mismatched_stems)
}
```

```{r write-assembled}
# Archive copy of the joined raw values, pre-rename
write_csv(indicators_assembled, file.path(dir_int, "indicators_assembled.csv"))
```

# 3. Indicator table for the app

Rename to app-facing names and order columns by the registry. One row per water
supply system.

```{r indicators-clean}
registry_present <- filter(indicator_registry, source_col %in% names(indicators_assembled))

indicators_clean <- indicators_assembled |>
  select(wsd_source_id, all_of(set_names(registry_present$source_col, registry_present$app_name))) |>
  distinct(wsd_source_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

dim(indicators_clean)
```

## Coverage check

```{r indicator-coverage}
# Non-missing count per indicator. A count far below the others usually means a
# genuine data gap, not a bug, but it is worth confirming before the app ingests it.
indicators_clean |>
  summarise(across(-wsd_source_id, ~ sum(!is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "app_name", values_to = "n_valid") |>
  mutate(pct_valid = round(100 * n_valid / nrow(indicators_clean), 1)) |>
  left_join(select(indicator_registry, app_name, pathway, component, factor), by = "app_name") |>
  arrange(n_valid) |>
  print(n = Inf)

# Completeness per supply: how many indicators each site actually contributes.
# NOTE: `na.rm = TRUE` in the app's rowSums() makes a missing indicator and an
# explicit zero mechanically identical, so sites low on this histogram score
# systematically lower. Accepted methodological choice, flagged here for QA.
indicators_clean |>
  mutate(n_indicators = rowSums(!is.na(across(-wsd_source_id)))) |>
  count(n_indicators) |>
  arrange(desc(n_indicators)) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

Saved twice: a date-stamped copy in `data/rapid/outputs/`, so each run is kept,
and the fixed-name copy the app reads (`app.R` and `deploy.R` refer to
`final_indicators.csv` by name).

```{r write-indicators}
write_csv(indicators_clean,
          file.path(dir_out, paste0("final_indicators_", Sys.Date(), ".csv")))
write_csv(indicators_clean, file.path(dir_app, "final_indicators.csv"))
```

## Source-type indicator weights

Each indicator applies to some water source types more than others: 1 = the
indicator fully applies to that source type, 0 = not at all. Two inputs:

-   `weights/indicator_weights.csv`: **the table to edit.** One row per
    indicator, one column per source category (`SWS` Streams & Rivers, `SWL`
    Lakes & Reservoirs, `SGW_SP` Springs & Shallow Groundwater, `DGW` Deep
    Groundwater, `RW` Rainwater, `O` Ocean).
-   `indicator_weights_<date>.csv`: each supply's source category
    (`weight_category`), written by `calc_indicator_weights()` in
    `rapid_workflow.Rmd`.

They are joined into one row per supply with a `wt_<indicator>` column per
indicator. The Methods Explorer multiplies each normalized indicator by its
weight (`normalized x model agreement x source-type weight`), so nothing is
applied to the raw values here. Supplies with no source category get no row and
are left unweighted. The deployed app does not use this file. To try other weights without knitting, use the Test
weights tab of the Methods Explorer in `nps_wsva_app/prototypes`.

```{r indicator-weights}
category_codes <- c(
  SWS    = "Streams & Rivers",
  SWL    = "Lakes & Reservoirs",
  SGW_SP = "Springs & Shallow Groundwater",
  DGW    = "Deep Groundwater",
  RW     = "Rainwater",
  O      = "Ocean"
)

indicator_weights <- read_csv("weights/indicator_weights.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

category_file <- latest_file("indicator_weights")
stopifnot(!is.na(category_file))
cat("Source categories from:", basename(category_file), "\n")

supply_categories <- read_csv(category_file, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  distinct(wsd_source_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Every scored indicator needs a weights row (model-agreement columns are
# confidence weights, not indicators), every weight must be 0-1, and every
# category label must be one of the six above.
scored <- setdiff(names(indicators_clean), "wsd_source_id") |>
  str_subset("_model_agree$", negate = TRUE)
weight_values <- as.matrix(indicator_weights[, names(category_codes)])

stopifnot(
  "Scored indicator(s) missing from weights/indicator_weights.csv" =
    all(scored %in% indicator_weights$app_name),
  "Duplicated app_name in weights/indicator_weights.csv" =
    !anyDuplicated(indicator_weights$app_name),
  "Weights must be numbers between 0 and 1" =
    is.numeric(weight_values) && !anyNA(weight_values) &&
    all(weight_values >= 0 & weight_values <= 1),
  "Unknown weight_category label in the source category file" =
    all(na.omit(supply_categories$weight_category) %in% category_codes)
)
setdiff(scored, indicator_weights$app_name)   # which ones, if the check above fails

# One row per source category, one wt_ column per indicator
category_weights <- indicator_weights |>
  select(app_name, all_of(names(category_codes))) |>
  pivot_longer(-app_name, names_to = "code", values_to = "weight") |>
  mutate(weight_category = unname(category_codes[code])) |>
  select(-code) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = app_name, values_from = weight, names_prefix = "wt_")

supply_indicator_weights <- supply_categories |>
  filter(!is.na(weight_category)) |>
  select(wsd_source_id, weight_category) |>
  left_join(category_weights, by = "weight_category")

count(supply_indicator_weights, weight_category, sort = TRUE)

# Supplies with indicators but no source category (left unweighted by the app)
indicators_clean |>
  filter(!wsd_source_id %in% supply_indicator_weights$wsd_source_id) |>
  pull(wsd_source_id)
```

```{r write-indicator-weights}
write_csv(supply_indicator_weights,
          file.path(dir_out, paste0("supply_indicator_weights_", Sys.Date(), ".csv")))
write_csv(supply_indicator_weights, file.path(dir_app, "supply_indicator_weights.csv"))
```

# 4. Water supplies

Built here, written at the end of section 5 once the state water rights
attributes have been attached. This is the only write of `water_supplies.csv`.

```{r water-supplies}
water_supplies <- get_wsd(rapid = TRUE) |>
  # some WSDs have NA source_state; fall back to the park-level `state` column
  mutate(source_state = if_else(is.na(source_state), state, source_state)) |>
  distinct(wsd_source_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

dim(water_supplies)
```

# 5. State water rights doctrine

Pulled from `explore_WaterRights_vulnerability.Rmd` (Parts 2a and 3). State
surface water and groundwater appropriation doctrines are joined to each supply
by `source_state` and carried as **descriptive** attributes only. They are not
scored or ranked, and they are not indicators.

The workbook covers CONUS only, so supplies in AK, HI, and the territories will
have `NA` doctrine fields by design.

> **DISCLAIMER (surface as-is in the app):** *The state water rights information
> is intended for general informational purposes only and should not be used as
> an alternative to seeking expert legal advice where necessary. Consult the
> state-specific State Engineer's Office and/or the applicable water resources
> governing body for any legal questions or advice related to water rights
> administration.*

```{r water-rights-state}
water_law <- read_excel("data/all/CONUS States_SW-GW_WaterManagement.xlsx",
                        sheet = "List") |>
  rename(state_name = State)

# Crosswalk state name (used by the workbook) to postal code (used by the WSD)
state_xwalk <- tigris::states(progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(source_state = STUSPS, state_name = NAME)

water_rights_state <- state_xwalk |>
  inner_join(water_law, by = "state_name") |>
  select(source_state, state_name, SurfaceWaterLaw, GroundWaterLaw,
         any_of("LegalFrameworkRef"))

# Any state in the workbook that failed to match a postal code
setdiff(water_law$state_name, water_rights_state$state_name)
```

```{r join-water-rights}
wr_cols <- setdiff(names(water_rights_state), "source_state")

water_supplies <- water_supplies |>
  select(-any_of(wr_cols)) |>   # keeps the chunk idempotent on re-run
  left_join(water_rights_state, by = "source_state")

# Supplies with no doctrine attached (expect AK / HI / territories only)
water_supplies |>
  filter(is.na(SurfaceWaterLaw)) |>
  count(source_state, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r write-water-supplies}
write_csv(water_supplies, file.path(dir_app, "water_supplies.csv"))
```

# 6. WBM / LOCA2 climate summary

```{r wbm-data}
wbm_file <- latest_file("loca2_climate_change_summary")
stopifnot(!is.na(wbm_file))
cat("Reading:", basename(wbm_file), "\n")

wbm_data <- read_csv(wbm_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Supply attributes to carry onto the spatial layer
supply_attrs <- water_supplies |>
  select(any_of(c("wsd_source_id", "park_unit", "park_name", "region",
                  "source_state", "water_system_name", "system_type",
                  "source_type", "source_longitude", "source_latitude")))

wbm_sf <- wbm_data |>
  # drop any duplicated attribute columns so the join cannot produce .x/.y
  select(-any_of(setdiff(names(supply_attrs), "wsd_source_id"))) |>
  left_join(supply_attrs, by = "wsd_source_id") |>
  filter(!is.na(source_longitude), !is.na(source_latitude)) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("source_longitude", "source_latitude"),
           crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

# Rows that could not be located (no match in the WSD, or missing coordinates)
cat("WBM rows:", nrow(wbm_data),
    "| located:", nrow(wbm_sf),
    "| unique supplies:", n_distinct(wbm_sf$wsd_source_id), "\n")

st_write(wbm_sf, file.path(dir_app, "wbm_data.gpkg"),
         delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
```

# 7. Municipal / hauled supplies

Full WSD (not the rapid subset), since these system types are excluded from the
scored set but still shown on the map.

```{r municipal-hauled}
municipal_hauled <- get_wsd() |>
  filter(str_detect(source_type,
                    regex("municipal|hauled|tribal|purchased", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  distinct(wsd_source_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  filter(!is.na(source_longitude), !is.na(source_latitude)) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("source_longitude", "source_latitude"),
           crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

st_write(municipal_hauled, file.path(dir_app, "municipal_hauled.gpkg"),
         delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)

nrow(municipal_hauled)
```
